newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER-DJETOU, LEGWINSKI RETURN TO ADD STEEL TO MONACO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DJETOU, LEGWINSKI RETURN TO ADD STEEL TO MONACO.

text.p: Promoted Chateauroux go from the frying pan into the fire when they visit champions Monaco in the French first division on Friday.
Last season's second division champions, given no easy introduction to the top flight, lost 2-0 at Paris St Germain, France's other European Cup entrants, on Saturday.

The trip to the principality is all the more daunting for the small club from central France as Monaco will be looking to rebound from a 1-0 defeat at Bordeaux last Friday in a flawed start to their defence.
Monaco will be strengthened by the return of defender Martin Djetou and midfielder Sylvain Legwinski, two key figures in their championship season, who missed the trip to Bordeaux through injury.
"We are recovering Leg and Djetou and they're going to give us a plus with their quality and combativeness," coach Jean Tigana said.
Legwinski, a potential member of France's 1998 World Cup squad, is keen to get back into action.
"A season full of challenges awaits us. We must quickly reassure ourselves by beating Chateauroux on Friday," he said.

Nigerian striker Victor Ikpeba said last week's match was "made harder by a good Bordeaux team and we didn't play well... We had a much better second half. Pity we conceded that goal right at the end of the match, we deserved a draw."
Bordeaux striker Lilian Laslandes scored the winner in the 89th minute.
"We know that the departure of Sonny (Anderson of Brazil) puts a lot of responsibility on the forwards who have remained and that's a motivation," Ikpeda said.
Fellow striker Thierry Henry said: "We're going to miss Sonny, that's sure, we'll have to overcome (the loss) and we'll have it all to prove.
"But let's be careful not to be over confident, Chateauroux have nothing to lose, they won't have any pressure, they held PSG for more than an hour on the first day."
